articles.headline: LeBron James and 76ers breeze past Pacers 111-87, advance to NBA Cup knockout round
articles.description: — LeBron James had 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists, and the Philadelphia 76ers breezed past the Indiana Pacers 111-87 on Friday night to win East Group B and advance to the knockout round of the
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — LeBron James had 21 points, seven rebounds and six assists, and the Philadelphia 76ers breezed past the Indiana Pacers 111-87 on Friday night to win East Group B and advance to the knockout round of the NBA Cup.


              Joel Embiid added 14 points and 11 rebounds for the Eastern Conference-leading Sixers (16-4), who have won seven of eight.


              James hit three 3-pointers in the opening four minutes and scored 11 points in the first quarter as the Sixers never trailed. He finished 8 of 13 from the floor in 27 minutes.


              Anfernee Simons added 19 points for Philadelphia, Tyrese Maxey scored 14 and Dominick Barlow had 12.


              Jay Huff scored 18 points and Andrew Nembhard added 14 for Indiana, which made its fewest 3-pointers of the season, going 5 of 37 (13.5%) from beyond the arc. The Pacers beat Oklahoma City on Monday night but have lost five of six.


              Ivica Zubac had 16 rebounds for Indiana.


              Philadelphia shot 15 of 37 (40.5%) from 3-point range.


              Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton is practicing with the team as he rehabs from a left hamstring strain but missed his 15th straight game. He last played on Oct. 26.


              Up next
              76ers: At Houston on Saturday night.


              Pacers: At Chicago on Saturday night.

articles.headline: Raptors beat Nets in final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams
articles.description: — Scottie Barnes scored 34 points and the Toronto Raptors beat the Brooklyn Nets 124-100 on Friday night in the final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams.
articles.body:
TORONTO -- — Scottie Barnes scored 34 points and the Toronto Raptors beat the Brooklyn Nets 124-100 on Friday night in the final NBA Cup group-stage game for both teams.


              The Raptors finished the game holding the Eastern Conference wild-card berth at 3-1, but dropped out when Atlanta beat Boston a few minutes later. The Celtics had a higher point differential than the Raptors.


              Immanuel Quickley had a triple-double with 24 points, a season-high 14 assists and 10 rebounds for Toronto (7-11). Collin Murray-Boyles came off the bench for 19 points and seven rebounds.


              Ja’Kobe Walter left the game in the third quarter because of a right quad contusion. He finished with three points, three rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes.


              Julius Randle and Mikel Brown Jr. scored 21 points apiece for Brooklyn (4-14). Michael Porter Jr. added 17 points.

articles.headline: Steelers, fueled by jabs over Aaron Rodgers drama, 'come together' to rout Broncos
articles.description: Turned into a national punchline following Aaron Rodgers' release, the Steelers played with a sense of "urgency" and "anger" Friday night in a 27-6 win over Denver.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- As the final seconds ticked off the scoreboard at Acrisure Stadium early Friday evening, Mason Rudolph shrugged off his oversized rain cape and hugged his teammates on the sideline. Nearby, other teammates embraced as the score went final -- a resounding 27-5 upset victory against the Denver Broncos, a team considered to be one of the AFC's elite.

The final score was an exhale for an organization and a fanbase that rode a roller coaster of unprecedented circumstances over the previous 72 hours, and it kept the Steelers squarely in the playoff picture.

"This was a must win," wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. said. "Because if we didn't win, then the s--- storm keeps brewing."

In a matter of days, one of the league's most respected franchises turned into a punchline as Aaron Rodgers torched head coach Mike McCarthy on national television following an ultimatum that led to the quarterback's benching and release.

While the outside reveled in the drama and laughed at their expense, the players in the building, led by Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt, closed ranks and found strength and fight in playing for each other and the organization.

"No one feels sorry for us," tight end Pat Freiermuth said. "And so we either come together or we look like fools on national television. I thought T.J. and Cam did a really good job before the game, really talking about it's bigger than one person, it's bigger than two people, it's bigger than -- it's about the Rooney family and the Steelers and the fans, and they deserve our best effort today."

To do that, the Steelers leaned on their veteran leaders. Freiermuth addressed the offense before the game, and Heyward and Watt followed with pregame messages to the entire team.

"Can't worry about yesterday," Heyward said, relaying the message he gave his teammates. "Can't worry about tomorrow. Just be present. When tough times happen, they're just right for us. We are built for this. We move on, and don't feel sorry for yourself.

"And I just think I can say those words, but I can't say enough good things about the men that believe in those. And TJ, Jalen [Ramsey]. Our leadership is built on not just one person, but a group of guys believing and just trusting each other."

And with a foundation of that trust, the Steelers came out of the tunnel with an extra shot of energy and shook off their streak of slow starts. They jumped out to a 14-0 first-quarter lead thanks to Watt's fumble recovery in the end zone on a dropped ball by Bo Nix and a 22-yard touchdown catch by embattled wide receiver DK Metcalf.

The crowd of more than 66,000 roared as Rudolph stepped on the field for the first snap of the game, and it popped again when Rudolph connected with Metcalf for a short pass on the second.

"Nobody's feeling sorry for us," linebacker Payton Wilson said. "So we have to go out there and prove it. And I think both sides of the ball, all three phases today did a really good job of just playing complementary ball,

articles.headline: Bo Nix, after one of his worst games for Broncos, says 'I let the team down'
articles.description: After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Steelers on Friday.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday. 

The Broncos' first Black Friday game certainly won't go in Nix's scrapbook -- or the offense's -- as the Broncos mustered just 205 net yards, as Nix's lone fumble was recovered for a touchdown and one of his two interceptions returned for a touchdown. 

"It's frustrating for sure, and I let the team down,'' Nix said. "[That is] the last thing I want to do as a quarterback, as a leader of the team. ... [My teammates] didn't let me get too down. I was wanting to get a little more down than they were letting me.''

In a game played in a steady rain with a wind chill of 29 degrees at kickoff, Nix finished 22-of-49 passing for 169 yards and was sacked three times, with the three turnovers. It was the first time in Nix's 47 career starts, including regular season and playoffs, that he had three turnovers and was sacked three times in the same game.

The struggles in the rain were reminiscent of a 10-9 win over the Jets in 2024, his rookie year; Nix finished with a career-low 60 yards passing at a rain-swept MetLife Stadium. 

The Broncos' 204 net yards Friday were their third fewest this season, trailing the 176 net yards in the season-opening loss at Kansas City and 168 in a Week 6 win over Seattle.

Broncos coach Sean Payton was quick to defend Nix, pointing the finger more at his playcalls that led to the first-half turnovers.

"Starts with me,'' Payton said. "Early on, we gave them opportunities with momentum, and that falls on me.''

Nix and Payton circled the QB's first-quarter fumble as one of those opportunities for the Steelers. The Steelers came into Friday's game after benching -- and eventually waiving -- quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who took aim at Steelers coach Mike McCarthy in an interview on "The Pat McAfee Show."

But in a scoreless game, with the Broncos' offense already sputtering, Denver faced a third-and-15 from its own 19-yard line. After the snap, the Broncos tried to set up a screen pass to running back Tyler Badie, but the Steelers had multiple defenders quickly beat blocks, and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton promptly dropped to get in the passing lane in front of Badie.

As Nix tried to reset after he saw Badie covered, he lost the ball, and T.J. Watt recovered it in the end zone. The touchdown brought the Steelers' crowd into full-throated support that never dissipated.

"Going down 7-0, with a fumble recovered for a touchdown is definitely not ideal,'' Nix said. "That started us off on the wrong foot, and we could never get out of the hole. ... Momentum is a real thing.''

"I'm kicking myself for the first score,'' Payton said. "You know, we're running a screen play, but it's a slower-developing screen play, and coming out [from near the end zone], that's not too good. ... This is one of those games, 10 points [Friday] is different than 10

articles.headline: Isaiah Joe scores 22 points, Pistons' reserves power NBA Cup win over Bucks
articles.description: — Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night.


              The Pistons wpn East Group A at 3-1 with a better points differential than the Toronto Raptors and Orlando Magic. Detroit will host a knockout-round game and could finish with the Eastern Conference's top seed.


              The Bucks finished 0-4 in group play.


              The Pistons, who finished with seven players in double figures, were missing three starters — Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) have been out for weeks, and Cade Cunningham (knee) also was in street clothes.


              Paul Reed and fellow reserve Elijah Harkless added 14 points. Detroit had 60 bench points while the starters finished with 53.


              Rookie Brayden Burries had 23 points for the Bucks and Tyler Herro added 20.


              Milwaukee led by 16 points in the first quarter, but only had a two-point advantage at halftime. The Pistons then put up a 42-point third quarter that included points from eight players. Daniss Jenkins' 3-pointer at the buzzer put Detroit up 90-78 at quarter's end.


              Officials and coaches had to jump in between the players midway through the fourth after Myles Turner fired a ball into Ausar Thompson's back. Both players were given technical fouls.


              After the confrontation, the game turned into a dunk fest for the Pistons, who got points from nine players in an 64-point second half.


              The Bucks had a rare good start, taking a 19-3 lead before Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff pulled all of his starters. The reserves got Detroit back into the game, then went on a 15-2 run to take the lead in the second quarter.


              Milwaukee led 50-48 at halftime, with Detroit's starters only contributing 12 points.


              Up next
              Bucks: Host Oklahoma City on Saturday night.


              Pistons: Host Orlando on Sunday night.

articles.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 12

Players with early starts

Derrick Henry, RB, Ravens (concussion): Henry had originally cleared the league's concussion protocol after last week's game, but had "small symptoms" and reentered the protocol Wednesday. He returned to practice in full capacity Thursday. He has since returned to full practice and is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 12. Fantasy managers should start him, even in a difficult matchup against the Texans.

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (ankle): Flowers was limited to start the practice week before being elevated to full participation Thursday. Though it is a bit worrisome, considering he dealt with ankle issues early this season, Flowers will play in Week 12. Though his ceiling is clearly lower without Lamar Jackson, he has still surpassed 11 points in two straight games. The volume he sees keeps him in play for fantasy managers.

Tee Higgins, WR, Bengals (hamstring): Tee Higgins reportedly woke up with soreness in his hamstring Friday and is questionable for Week 12. Zac Taylor said that Higgins should be fine for Sunday's game. Though it is an added risk that fantasy managers would rather avoid, Higgins is a "must-start" whenever active.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 12 Buzz

articles.headline: Sam Darnold 'ready to roll' vs. 49ers as Seahawks fight to stay in NFC West race
articles.description: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold, who missed the past two games with a quad injury, will return to start against the Niners in a pivotal NFC West showdown.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- After playing through a cracked rib and then missing the past two games because of a quad injury, quarterback Sam Darnold is back in the Seattle Seahawks' starting lineup in time for their most pivotal matchup of the season.

Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Friday that Darnold will start Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium, a game the Seahawks must win to keep any realistic hope alive of staying in the NFC West race.

"I feel really good," Darnold said Friday after practicing as a full participant for the third straight day. "I'm not going to compare it to any other point in the season, but I feel really good right now."

The Seahawks ruled out right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe). In addition to Darnold, they'll get left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) back.

Macdonald had said earlier in the week that the plan was for Darnold to start against the 49ers (9-1) as long as all went well Wednesday in a full-speed practice that followed a lighter session the Seahawks (6-4) had Monday as they returned from their bye.

"Sam did a great job," Macdonald said. "We got through Wednesday, so we're ready to roll."

Said offensive coordinator Brian Fleury: "He looked great, honestly. It's hard to believe he missed a few weeks and was not throwing and stuff like that. They did a great job with him during the bye week, making sure he was going to be ready to go, and so he looks fantastic."

Darnold missed the Seahawks' wins over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 and Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 because of a quad injury he suffered near the end of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. Darnold also suffered a cracked rib against the Bears on his first dropback of the night.

Darnold said "everyday-life things," such as lying in bed, were difficult for several days because of his cracked rib, but that he could throw shortly after suffering the injury. He said he could have continued to play through it, as he did against Chicago, if not for the quad injury.

"There's times throughout the season where you're going to have to play through a little bit of pain, but I've dealt with stuff like that throughout every season," he said. "I'm sure everyone does. So, that's just something you've got to deal with sometimes, and I felt like it was manageable to be able to go out there and still perform to a level to where I felt like it was important to be out there."

Darnold said he'll have a bit of extra rib padding Sunday but that it won't be too different from what he normally wears.

Darnold hurt his quad while escaping the pocket to avoid a blitzing linebacker on Seattle's second-to-last play against the Bears. He said he had to replicate that kind of movement to know that he was ready to return.

articles.headline: Alonso urges Chelsea to 'stick together' amid run of three losses
articles.description: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said his team should "stick together" after a 3-2 loss to Nottingham Forest on Friday made it three Premier League defeats in a row for the Stamford Bridge side.
articles.body:
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said his team should "stick together" after a 3-2 loss to Nottingham Forest on Friday made it three Premier League defeats in a row for the Stamford Bridge side.

Igor Jesus scored a spectacular opener for the hosts at the City Ground before Wesley Fofana's reckless foul on Liam Delap allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to double Forest's lead.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice for Chelsea to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that did not change the complexion of a game in which Fofana was loudly booed by Chelsea's travelling fans and was subbed off soon after his foul on Delap.

"Well, we have to stick together, and everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed," Alonso said. "We need to help, and we need to go through these tough moments all together, and we don't leave anyone apart.

"We need to support everyone. That is because we need everyone, and we need the fans. We need all the players. We need to stick together because if not, things will get more complicated, and that's what we want to do."

Asked whether the Chelsea fans' reaction, where Fofana was booed throughout and subjected to derogatory chants, made it more difficult to pick him going forward, Alonso added: "Well, I'm thinking right after the game and for the next games, we will see."

Fofana's situation is just one of a growing list of issues for Alonso to deal with as they slide down the table.

Jesus' brilliant opening goal, an acrobatic volley into the top corner, put Forest ahead and they doubled the lead when Gibbs-White struck from the spot.

Emegha got Chelsea back into it, with their first shot on target, but the hosts restored their two-goal lead when Gibbs-White latched on to Xaver Schlager's fine pass.

Emegha's late second set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

But the Austrian is not getting carried away.

"It looks like we are progressing, and this is what we all want to see," Glasner said. "But also, I said last time it was the first swallow, and now it's the second swallow, and I think everybody could feel it tonight, we are far away from summer!

"So staying humble, take this feeling of the win and the confidence and the belief, but staying humble and prepare well for Hull because we have three-game week before we face Brighton.

"After the three-game week we can summarise."

Chelsea, who ended the day in 8th place, host Crystal Palace in their next match, while 14th-placed Forest are away to Hull City. Both games are on Dec. 2.

Information from PA was used in this report.

articles.headline: Wesley Fofana booed by Chelsea fans against Nottingham Forest over interview comments
articles.description: Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after his controversial unauthorized interview.
articles.body:
Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after his controversial unauthorised interview and endured a harrowing night on the pitch at the City Ground.

The centre-back gave away a penalty for a rash foul that was converted by Morgan Gibbs-White and was susbequently substituted by Xabi Alonso before the hour-mark in the game.

The Blues defender drew criticism earlier in the week for talking for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics, admitting that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

Fofana apologised for the interview and boss Xabi Alonso said the matter was closed, but visiting supporters were less forgiving.

They jeered their own player when he was in possession.

- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving

- Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners

It has been a particularly difficult spell for Fofana, who has been singled out for poor performances during the team's bad run. His poor form carried into the City Ground, where his error and subsequent foul on Liam Delap saw him concede a penalty early in the second-half.

Chelsea had endured a tough start at the City Ground as they fell behind to Igor Jesus' brilliant fifth-minute strike. Gibbs-White's penalty doubled the hosts' lead soon after the break. 

Fofana's foul on Delap earned him a booking and led to Alonso taking him off in the 56th minute in favour of Levi Colwill. 

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Is Arsenal-Man City still the biggest PL match of the season?
articles.description: Arsenal vs. Man City was supposed to be the Premier League's marquee fixture, but it feels anything but in light of City's guilty verdict. What does Sunday's game really mean?
articles.body:
Two Premier League title contenders face each other Sunday, with one of the sides simultaneously favorites to be relegated. This is the bizarre state of flux that English football's top division now finds itself in.

Arsenal versus Manchester City is the biggest game of the 2026-27 season to date, but chances are it will have only a negligible bearing on the outcome of the title race. Three points, as always, is the prize, yet many people -- including the bookmakers -- expect City to receive a sporting punishment that dwarfs that figure after being found guilty on 114 counts of breaking Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period up to 2018.

Sanctions ranged from expulsion to a huge points deduction and a record fine. City continue to strongly protest their innocence, and an appeal over the guilty verdicts is expected to be heard next month. In the meantime, we are all asked to pretend this is just another normal season with usual rhythm, the usual ebb and flow.

Managers Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca certainly sought to give that impression in their prematch news conferences Friday.

"I think when we have two teams at the level that they are both at right now, with the quality players they have on that pitch, it is a massive game and a big game to enjoy I think," said Arteta, noting "that's the only thing we that should put the energy and focus in, there is nothing else."

Said Maresca: "Sunday is important, 100%, but for us it is a long season. We will see February and March where we are and from there you can set up the goals. Now I think it's useless to speak about targets or where we can be at the end of the season."

But what is the mood behind the scenes in both camps really like? And what does this game really mean?

Arsenal need a statement win

There is little love lost between these two sides, and a genuine rivalry has formed on the pitch as Arsenal cemented their status as City's principal challengers in recent years before finally snatching the crown last season. Watch Erling Haaland and Gabriel Magalhães go at it once again this weekend as they always do.

Sources have also suggested City have grown skeptical of Arsenal off the field over the years, perhaps dating back to the Gunners snatching Arteta from Pep Guardiola's coaching staff in December 2019. Recent tensions between City and many other Premier League clubs over the whole charges saga have done little to quell such ill feelings.

Arsenal are, in theory, the team that stands to benefit most from City's potential demise.
